content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file carefully in one pass without testing, designing a correct-by-construction model for an elven ranger archer with realistic proportions, standing in a rest pose with arms angled outward, and planning the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hips.

Working through this, I'm laying out the full joint chain from spine to head and arms, and deciding how to handle fingers—settling on a manageable scheme of five digits per hand with two joints each to keep the joint count reasonable. Now I'm computing the leg proportions and IK limb targets for hips, knees, and ankles, working out lengths and bend directions so the chain reaches the foot position correctly.

I'm adding a toe joint parented to the ankle for foot geometry, and settling on using world coordinates directly rather than fighting with the side convention from the docs—so side "L" just maps to positive X. Now I'm building the spine chain upward from the hips root joint through several vertebrae to the chest, making sure the first spine joint aligns with the hips socket position.

I'm then working out the neck and head structure, deciding to create the head as its own separate joint parented off the neck tip rather than folding it into the neck chain, with a bone direction aimed upward and slightly back, and committing to specifying all positions in world coordinates throughout to avoid confusion with local axes.

Now I'm moving to the arms, parenting the neck chain off the spine's last joint, then sketching an A-pose arm rig with shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions computed as offsets along diagonal direction vectors for upper arm, forearm, and hand lengths.

I'm defining a tapered radius profile for the arm sweep and deciding to build the limb curve through a catmull-rom spline across the three joint points, since that gives smooth rounded skinning compared to a sharp polyline. Then I start thinking about shoulder armor styling for the elven ranger look.

For the back piece, I settle on a single spaulder on the left shoulder plus a flowing cloak with a hood down, using a membrane stretched between a shoulder-line edge and a hem edge rather than a loft, keeping the cloak offset behind the body so it won't clip through the legs.

Defining membrane paint colors...

For bone structure, I'll attach a chest joint around the spine tip near 1.45 for cloak attachment. For hair, I'm planning long silver-blonde braided anime-style hair with a main hair cap mass behind the head plus long trailing braids.

Checking positions, I realize a straight-down braid would intersect the cloak geometry near the back, so instead I'll drape the braid diagonally over the left shoulder toward the chest for a more elegant look, mapping out joint points from the nape down across the shoulder to the front.

I'll use "tail" as the role even though it's a braid, and parent it to the head joint since parenting to chest would be better physically but head keeps things simpler for now.

For the hair, I'm planning a large sweeping cap from crown to behind the neck using a sphere-like part scaled over the head, colored to match the hair.

For the head shape, I'm sizing the skull as an ellipsoid sphere roughly 0.085-0.105-0.1 in radii, positioned to match a stylized anime proportion (7.5 heads tall for a 1.85m body), with a separate smaller wedge piece for the lower jaw and cheek shaping to get the elongated facial look right. I'm also adding pointed elf ears as extruded leaf shapes angled back-up-out, side locks framing the face, and bangs as extruded spike cards.

I'm working out the chin and jaw geometry so the lower jaw sphere joins seamlessly with the skull to form a believable chin, checking that their overlap at the bottom and front z-depth lines up correctly, then placing the mouth as a thin decal line and figuring out eye placement using surface decals anchored by azimuth angle on the skull front.

For the eyes, I'm calculating the azimuth and elevation offsets needed to position them symmetrically near the top-front of the skull, applying a mirror rule so the creature's left eye flips correctly, and making sure bangs are placed high enough not to cover them. I'm also adding a small forward-pointing nose cone and planning a tiny mouth shape near the chin.

I'm now working out where exactly the jaw and skull surfaces meet to place a believable mouth line, comparing the protrusion depths of the jaw sphere versus the skull ellipse at different heights to figure out where a small smile mark should sit.

Still working out the surface positions...

Now I'm thinking through the ear geometry - elf ears need an outline swept outward and back with an upward point, so I'm setting up the local coordinate frame with the drawing plane oriented back-and-up and thickness running along x.

Still working out the ear geometry...

That checks out with the x and y directions being orthogonal, confirming the ear shape math works. Now thinking about accessories and coloring: small gold earrings, and for the hair I'm considering a pale gold-silver tone with the overall elven ranger palette of forest green cloak, brown leather, and gold/teal accents.

Let me nail down the actual color palette: pale peach skin, pale cream hair with a tan shadow tone, two shades of green for the cloak, brown and dark brown for leather, flat gold for accents, cream for the tunic, and a teal glow for magical highlights on the bow runes and gem pendant. The cel shading approach uses the surface normal against a fixed light direction to determine shadow versus highlight regions.

Now I'm thinking through the torso build -- lofting the body along the spine using bone-driven stations, with width running along the side-to-side axis and depth running front-to-back, starting from the hip measurements and working upward.

Working through waist, ribs, shoulders, and neck station values, matching the loft path to the spine chain's start point near the hips so the bone binding aligns properly. I'm also flagging that the pelvis region might need a separate shape for the hips/butt since the legs attach at a slight offset from center.

For the pelvis loft I'm sizing the starting station small enough that the rounded cap doesn't bulge too dramatically below the hip line, since that dome will get hidden under trousers and tunic anyway—settling on a modest width and height so the cap radius stays reasonable while still looking natural under the clothing layers.

Now I'm thinking through torso coloring: rather than a single paint, I want the shirt to be cream linen with a green leather jerkin layered over it, using a y-based paint function so the collar area shows cream while the body reads as green tunic.

For the lower body, I'm sketching a lathed skirt as a short tabard with flared panels in green and a leather hem, but worried the skirt radius might be too narrow relative to the legs poking through, so I'm widening the hip radius to make sure the legs stay hidden underneath.

I'm checking that the skirt hem radius at the knee height comfortably clears the thigh width, then noticing the cloak placed behind the body could intersect the back of the skirt and cause z-fighting, so I'm adjusting the cloak's depth and hem position to pull it further back and avoid the collision.

Rather than a full lathed skirt mesh, I'm reconsidering a simpler approach — maybe add a leather belt with a buckle and pouches, a quiver on the back, and a bow in hand instead.

Thinking through the bow pose: holding it in the left hand, pointing down at ease like a classic archer stance. Given realistic bow length around 1.5-1.6m and grip position near the hand at y≈0.97, the lower limb would extend well past the floor, so I need to position the grip high enough that the lower tip just touches the ground at y≈0.02.

A full longbow of that length means the upper tip reaches nearly 1.7-1.9m, which feels too tall for the figure's height, so I'm leaning toward a slightly shorter elven-style bow (~1.7m) with asymmetric limb lengths—lower limb shorter, upper limb longer—letting the grip sit lower-third rather than centered, like a staff planted at an angle. I'm now sketching the bow's curve as a swept profile in the YZ plane with control points defining the tip, grip, and upper limb positions.

Working out the left arm pose so the hand grips the bow naturally in front of the body, I'm placing explicit shoulder, elbow, and wrist coordinates to get a believable bent-forearm angle, then setting the grip point and curving the limbs forward slightly to suggest a recurve bow shape typical of elven design.

Working out the z-coordinates along the limb curve so the tips bend toward the archer while the grip stays further forward.

Checking the bowstring geometry — it should run nearly straight between the tip points, pulled back behind the grip to create a realistic brace height. I'll adjust the lower limb tips to smaller z values so the string sits closer to the archer with roughly a .17 brace distance from the grip.

For the right arm, I'm keeping it relaxed at the archer's side: shoulder, elbow, and wrist positioned down toward the belt, hand open and loosely curled rather than holding anything. The arrows will instead sit in a quiver across the back, with fletching cards to suggest feathers.

Now I'm working out quiver placement so it clears the cloak properly—computing the cloak's z-offset at shoulder height and shifting the quiver axis outward so it sits visibly over rather than buried under the cloak fabric.

For the baldric strap, I'm thinking I should skip trying to drape it precisely over the chest surface and instead approximate it as a simple rod or sweep running diagonally from one shoulder to the opposite hip.

Finishing the back-strap points, I realize they extend beyond the torso surface at the back, so the drape will snap them inward to the cloak's position, effectively hiding the strap under the cloak membrane. That raises the question of where the quiver attaches since it's normally held by that now-hidden strap — I'll consider hanging it at the hip instead.

Simplicity wins here: I'll give the quiver its own visible strap looping over the right shoulder to the front chest, and simplify the cloak into a hooded mantle that drapes only from the shoulders down rather than wrapping the whole back.

Continuing the strap path down to where it disappears under the belt, crossing just above the cloak's top edge at the shoulder. I'll give it a flat band-like cross section rather than a round cord, roughly 0.017 by 0.006 in radius, swept along the path.

I'm second-guessing exact depth placement against the torso surface — at chest height the body's half-depth suggests the strap center should sit around z=0.11–0.125 to clear the surface without floating too much. Rather than hand-tuning each point, I'll just let the front/shoulder portion drape directly onto the torso surface and leave the back portion free-floating, snapping the points to the nearest surface where needed.

I'm simplifying the quiver strap to two segments: a short free polyline from the quiver top up to near the shoulder, then a draped segment following the cloak's surface from there. To keep risk low since I can't test runtime behavior, I'm sticking to a small set of API calls I'm confident about — builder creation, joints, chains, sweeps, and parts — rather than improvising new ones.

I'm also thinking through color handling: using cel-shaded Paint for major surfaces versus flat colors for small details, while watching that painting too many parts doesn't overload the texture atlas, and deciding whether gold accents should also get the cel treatment for consistency.

With part counts staying well under the limit, I'm moving on to the actual coordinate design — setting up helper functions for spheres and placing parts relative to bones, then sketching overall proportions in world space, aiming for roughly 1.9 meters total height including hair and headwear, with the head centered around y=1.74.

Now I'm placing the feet and legs: boot sole resting at floor level, ankle joint positioned forward near the toe, and figuring out how to sweep the boot shaft along the shin using a colored sweep from the leg chain so it reads as a calf boot below the knee.

I'm working out the leg's radius profile along its sweep -- tapering from hip through knee down to ankle using interpolated radius values at each chain point.

Checking the leg geometry, the hip-to-ankle distance leaves room for a subtle knee bend, with the forward offset coming out to about 0.163, giving a natural slight bend rather than a straight rigid leg.

Now I'm working through how the limb helper function handles the bend direction parameter, deciding to pass a single bend vector wrapped appropriately for the two-segment leg chain so the knee joint bends forward correctly.

Working out the naming convention for left/right sides and adding toe joints as children of the ankle, trying to figure out whether toes should use a "digit" role versus the standard chain roles already defined.

For getting the ankle joint, I'm just indexing directly into the chain's joints array rather than adding a helper function or extra type import, since the chain always ends with hip, knee, ankle in order.

Now I'm sketching the boot geometry: a heel-to-toe sweep along the ankle bone forming the sole, with a separate rounded toe cap swept along the toe bone, using tapering elliptical radii and a darker color for the cap.

Still shaping the toe curve and radius tapering...

For the toe sweep, I'm raising the endpoint y-value so the tip curls upward above the floor, giving it an elven pointed look, and then moving on to the boot shaft paint logic and a cuff fold near the knee.

For the cuff I'm weighing lathe versus sweep approaches, since the shin tilts forward toward the knee, making a simple vertical lathe inadequate -- leaning toward using a surface loop method tied to the leg sweep instead.

Since chain.at(t) gives me a Frame along the bone, I can place the cuff about 72% down the shin and use that frame to drive a loop sweep for the band.

I'm thinking I can add matching bracers on the arms using the same loop-and-sweep technique, and maybe a belt around the hips, but the hip joint's default orientation isn't aligned to the bone so I'd need to supply an explicit up-direction frame instead of relying on the joint axis.

I'm unsure about the frame orientation for a horizontal closed belt path, so I'll just use a safe rope-like radius of .018 for the leather belt plus a buckle and pouches. Now I'm planning out the overall part structure and figuring out which imports I'll actually need before writing the final code.

Defining skin and hair color palettes...

Settling on dark olive leggings, and now I'm working out the cloak's paint function: gold trim near the hem edge, a darker trim band just above it, and a gradient base color elsewhere on the membrane.

Adding fold bands and scalloped hem...

For the hood, I'll add a soft ellipsoid shape piled at the back of the neck in cloak color, plus a gold brooch clasp with a small glowing gem at the throat.

I'm working out a gold neck chain made from a closed catmull ring swept around the neck at the correct radius and position, attaching it to the neck1 bone, then placing the front brooch as a gold leaf shape with an inset teal glowing gem sphere positioned against the neck surface.

Now I'm pinning down the torso loft stations with catmull-interpolated centers through hips, waist, ribs, chest, and neck base, each with specific width and depth values to shape the body's curvature, and figuring out where the shoulder joints attach for the arms.

I need to balance the shoulder ball sphere radius against the arm socket so they overlap naturally, and taper the trapezius slope from the wide chest station down to the narrow neck base—that transition is quite steep, so I might need an intermediate station to smooth it out.

I'm also checking the spine bone chain coverage: since the chain only spans up to the chest joint, anything past that (like the neck base) gets owned entirely by the last bone, which should still work fine for the loft.

Then I'm wiring up the loft call itself to use that spine chain for bone-based deformation, and sketching out the paint function that colors the torso -- cream for the collar region above the neckline, green tunic fabric for the main body, with separate shading for the chest front.

For surface detail I'm avoiding anything resembling a logo or emblem, instead planning a decorative svg decal with criss-cross lacing down the front and gold filigree vine trim along the edges. Writing SVG decal code...

For the torso paint, I'm defining zones by height and width—cream collar up top, darker tunic shading for side panels, lighter tunic elsewhere—keeping it simple without separate ink outlines.

Now for the arm chain: I'm setting up shoulder-elbow-wrist joints as a named chain rooted at the chest, then building the hand as a palm capsule extending from the wrist along the forearm direction, sized appropriately for the knuckle region.

For fingers, I'm defining each digit as its own small three-joint chain (base, mid, tip) to keep motion simple, giving five fingers per hand roughly 15 joints each, well within budget, and sweeping thin capsule radii along each finger chain while parenting them to the wrist.

For positioning the left hand around the bow grip, I'm simplifying to a relaxed open hand with fingers semi-curled rather than a tight fist, letting the bow pass loosely through the curl, and I'm working out the shoulder-elbow-wrist vector geometry to place the wrist joint correctly for this arm.

I'm reconsidering where to place the bow grip relative to the knuckles so the fingers curl naturally around it, trying to set finger base positions using the knuckle point plus lateral offsets across the hand's width.

To simplify, I'm just picking a lateral axis for the fingers directly—orienting the palm inward for the left hand and spacing the four fingers along that direction, rather than deriving it precisely from the forearm geometry.

Working out the hand orientation vectors...

Working through the cross product, I find the right-hand version lands on the back side, meaning the handedness flips there, while redoing the same calculation for the left hand correctly gives a front-facing vector. So I need to apply a sign multiplier depending on hand to get consistent orientation.

Now I'm laying out the finger geometry: assigning lateral width offsets for index, middle, ring, and pinky across the hand's total width, segment lengths for each finger, and computing each segment's base position and curl direction by rotating the forward vector toward the palm normal at increasing bend angles.

I need to figure out where the bow should sit relative to the curled fingers so it actually passes through the grip loop naturally, since the fingers curl inward toward the palm and the bow needs to intersect that hollow rather than collide with the fingertips.

The fingers curling through x .36-.42 overlap the bow at .382, which reads fine as a loose grip even with the palm tilted 35° off the bow axis. I'll simplify by relaxing the right hand and having the left hand do the actual gripping, with the bow passing through x=.382, z=.184 at grip height y=.885.

Still mapping out the bow's curve points...

Feet rest at floor level so the minimum height is satisfied there, with the bow tip floating slightly above. For the string, I'm checking its path from the lower tip to the top tip doesn't collide with the forearm or hand given the limb geometry and string offset—the clearance works out fine. Now I'm working out the bow's wood sweep and grip wrap with a leather-wound riser section.

Writing limb taper and gold inlay bands...

Mapping out the full symmetric band list now, with gold tip and bands, wood segments, and a leather grip section around the midpoint, using flat paint for gold and cel shading for wood.

For the bow details, I'm adding small glowing teal rune gems on the limbs, attaching the bow to the wrist joint so it follows arm movement, and setting up a back-mounted quiver cylinder for arrows.

Checking the quiver's position against the cloak geometry, there's a slight overlap near the bottom that's fine since it's embedded, but near the top there's a small gap of about .05 units between the cloak and quiver surface that I'll bridge with strap geometry to visually pin them together.

I'm narrowing the quiver placement to tighten that top gap to just .02, attaching the cloak to move with the chest bone joint rather than the full spine so the legs don't disturb it. For the quiver mesh itself, I'm building a tapered rod shape between two points with slightly varying radius and leather coloring, sweeping a circular cross-section along the rod's length.

Now I'm working out colored bands along the quiver rod—gold and leather-dark rings at different points along its length to break up the leather surface—and adding a dark disc cap at the top to suggest the open mouth of the quiver.

For the arrows poking out the top, I'm planning five thin wooden shafts angled slightly outward from inside the quiver, each extending up past the rim, with small feather-shaped vanes near the top end rendered as thin colored cards or extruded blades for the fletching.

Cross:true doubles that into four fins, and I'll texture them with a feather-shaped SVG using barbs in teal-white, reused across one shared texture for all six arrow frames. For the arrow shafts themselves, I'm positioning them emerging from inside the quiver using the quiver's top-bottom axis, offsetting along that axis and spreading them laterally with a perpendicular basis vector.

Now I'm working out the lateral offsets and height variations for each arrow, plus small glowing nocks at the tips. I'm also planning the belt accessories: a leather belt with gold buckle, hip pouches, a sheathed dagger on the right hip, and hanging tassels, positioning them around the waist station.

Working out pouch placement...

For the belt, I need a surface query on the torso sweep so I can loop a strap around it and attach a gold buckle via a stick cylinder at the front hit point.

For the pauldron, I'm thinking of overlapping leaf-shaped plates fanning across the shoulder, placed on hits against a partial hemisphere shell since the arm sweep starts with a round cap there—though I'm unsure whether these part meshes render single or double-sided.

Still working out dome plate outlines...

I'm placing three plates along the shoulder-to-elbow line with increasing scale outward (1.0 to 1.25) and tilting axes progressively, attached to the arm's shoulder joint bone so they follow the raise motion, sized so their radius comfortably covers the arm's width at the shoulder.

For the bracers, I'm building a layered band of leather rings with gold accents clustered around the forearm's three-quarter point, using multiple adjacent thin loops to create a ridged leather texture with gold rings bracketing the ends for a cheap but convincing look.

Now I'm positioning a hair cap sphere set back and up from the skull center so it doesn't intrude on the face, working out the radii and offsets needed to keep the forehead and front face area clear while still covering the top and back of the head, checking where the hair silhouette meets the skull's front contour.

Then I'm sketching bangs as tapered curved locks sweeping from the crown down across the forehead, defining each lock as a tapered tube path from a crown point to a forehead endpoint sitting just outside the skull surface, sized so the tips land slightly beyond the scalp.

Working out side locks position...

I'm reconsidering back hair as a long sweeping fall from crown to mid-back, but worried it may collide with the cloak at the neck and shoulder region, so maybe the hair should rest on top of the cloak instead.

Simplifying: I'll make the back hair shorter, a tapered mass sweeping from crown to nape ending around y 1.55, shaped as a flattened ellipse that narrows toward the bottom, while keeping a separate front braid over the shoulder.

Now adding a ring of pointed anime-style spikes behind the shoulders at the end of the nape mass, plus a braid over the left shoulder tied with gold, and computing a gold circlet band as a closed elliptical ring across the forehead sized to match the head's cross-section at that height.

I'm also placing a small glowing teal gem in a gold setting at the circlet's front center, checking the geometry so it sits just outside the skull surface and that bangs properly layer over or under the circlet.

Working out the bangs path so strands flow from the crown down past the circlet toward the forehead, with tips ending near the top of the eyes.

For the remaining face details, I'm planning a tiny nose spike in skin tone, treating eyebrows as part of the anime eye decal, confirming elven ear tips poke through the hair, and setting the neck to use a chain sweep with skin-toned paint for proper shading. Now I'm starting the skull geometry as a scaled sphere part.

For the eye decals, I'm casting rays from the skull's surface center at slight angle offsets to find hit points, handling cases where the ray might miss, and placing eye decals at those positions with a small size, working out the vertical eye height from the skull's elevation angle.

I'm checking the horizontal spacing between the eyes and nose to make sure they don't overlap, adjusting the azimuth angle outward slightly to widen the eye placement relative to the face width.

Settling on an emerald-teal iris color for the eyes to match the character's elf-like glow accents. The mouth stays closed so no teeth or tongue are needed, and I'm structuring the jaw as a separate lower sphere attached at the jawbone, with the skull sphere forming the upper face so the seam lines up naturally at the mouth line, plus a small rosy patch for the lower lip.

Moving on to the cloak and hood, I'm picking two layered green tones for cel-shading and planning gold clasp details, then starting to sketch the lathe outline for the tunic skirt as a closed polygon loop with inner and outer hem points.

Checking that polygon for self-intersection, I realize the skirt hem may collide with the thigh geometry -- the legs poke outward past the skirt's inner radius near the hip area, so I need to widen the skirt top or narrow the thighs to fix the clipping.

Checking the leg clearance at that height confirms the skirt radius still clears the legs. I'm thinking through the skirt coloring with a gold hem band near the bottom transitioning to the darker tunic shade above it, and considering whether to add a zigzag or leaf-shaped hem for visual interest, though a full front slit cut seems too complex and I'll likely skip it.

Writing zigzag hem logic...

Now I'm working out leg geometry: boots, trousers, and cuff placement using world y-coordinates, computing knee position along the hip-to-ankle line with a forward perpendicular offset to find where the boot cuff sits.

I'll color the boots with a tan leather tone and gold trim at the cuff. For the remaining accessories, I'm skipping tassels in favor of a small hanging leaf charm, and planning a dagger sheathed at the right hip, positioned along the skirt's surface near the belt line.

The sheath end at x=-.205 actually lands inside the skirt's radius at that height, so I need to push it further out to x=-.26 to clear the skirt surface. Tracing the path from hilt to scabbard tip against the skirt's radius function confirms x=-.238 at y=.85 stays just outside the boundary.

Then for the hilt itself, I'm placing a gold pommel sphere above the grip and setting the hilt's cylinder axis to follow the same direction vector as the sheath, extended upward from the grip to pommel.

Now I'm moving on to defining the hand and finger geometry, starting with the relaxed right hand and curling thumb segments relative to the wrist position and palm normal.

I'm naming each finger joint with a consistent pattern (digit, segment index, side) so they attach correctly to the arm chain, and considering whether to add small fingernail details as tiny scaled spheres.

For jewelry, I'm planning a necklace with a curved chain of small gold points draped across the chest, ending in a teal gem pendant positioned against the torso's front surface — working out the z-depth of the chest at different heights so the chain sits flush against the body.

For the cloak attachment, I'm dropping the idea of a separate brooch and instead using two shoulder clasps connected by a sagging gold chain across the upper chest, simplifying how the cloak fastens at the front.

Adding teal magical glows on bow runes, quiver arrowheads, circlet gem, pendant, and arrow nocks, plus leaf-shaped glow motifs on bracers. No ground base needed since this is a character piece, and I'll skip the shoulder mantle beyond the pauldrons. For cloak decoration, embroidered gold vine patterns could work, but painted hem patterns should suffice without needing extra decal geometry.

Checking part count and triangle budget stays under 60k, fine. For hair, I'm sweeping a braid with an alternating zigzag paint pattern between two hair colors, tapering the radius along a chain of points, with small gold ring ties at two positions along the braid.

Still tuning the braid radius taper...

Checking that ChainPoint qualifies as a valid frame input for positioning parts. Now I'm working on the hood placement at the nape, noticing it conflicts with the hair spike geometry, so I'm adjusting the hair endpoint and hood center/radius to avoid overlap before moving on to positioning the arms near the torso.

Shoulder joints and arm sphere coverage at the chest width look fine, and the waist sash design is settled. Now I'm setting up the imports for the character builder—frame, limb, path utilities, paint, texture, and toon/glow kits—then defining the metadata block for the Elven Ranger Archer character.

Setting up the build function and color palette...

Building the hips root joint and spine chain hierarchy...

Still defining head and jaw joints...

I'm checking that the head's position sits correctly relative to the skull center and neck top, making sure the chin area aligns within the expected z-offset range.

Now I'm setting up the neck sweep with tapered radii so the cap rounds nicely into the skull, then starting the leg-building loop that mirrors hip positions for left and right sides using the limb helper.

I'm chaining the hip, knee, and ankle joints into a leg structure parented to the hips, then thinking through foot joint placement next.

Still writing joint and sweep definitions...

The neck base dome and collar details check out fine, extending from the chest tip into the neck region. I'm now adding a cream collar ring around the neck base and a standing leaf-shaped collar for the tunic, positioning them where the torso cross-section still exists.

Moving to torso decals, I'm setting up a surface reference on the torso, then adding a leather belt loop at waist height with gold studs distributed along the path, using frame-based positioning so the studs inherit proper orientation from the belt curve.

For the buckle, I'm casting a ray forward from the torso surface to find the front-facing hit point, then attaching the buckle geometry there conditionally once the hit is confirmed.

Still working out pouch geometry...

Working out the geometry for the flap and pouch placement, I'm calculating that a 15° elevation hits the torso roughly .03 higher, so the flap stick should sit at azimuth 65, elevation 14. I'm now checking that the pouch box (protruding ~.0375) and the flap box (thin at .016) don't overlap in z, since the flap's position seems to land inside the pouch's protrusion range rather than cleanly above it.

Adjusting the flap box dimensions slightly larger so it protrudes a bit more than the pouch, which should give a cleaner layered look -- pouch in leather color, flap in a darker leather shade. I'm placing a second smaller pouch further back on the side, then moving on to defining the cloak's membrane geometry with its top and hem edge point arrays.

I'm checking clearance between the cloak's draped edges and the arm at the elbow -- interpolating the cloak's width and z-depth at that height to confirm the arm swings outside the cloak boundary in the A-pose stance.

I'm then verifying the quiver and bow positions sit within the cloak's open z-range without overlap, and checking the torso's back curve against the cloak's center-line depth at shoulder and chest heights -- the gaps stay around .03, which should be enough separation. I'm also confirming the shoulder sphere collider stays outside the cloak's top edge point by a safe margin before moving on to check the hip area clearance.

Now I'm sketching the cloak's hem coloring logic, defining a scalloped edge threshold based on position along the cloak surface to decide where the gold trim paints in versus the base fabric color.

Still defining cloak zones...

Computing the arrow's orientation axis and perpendicular vectors to set up a local coordinate frame for positioning the arrowhead.

Placing each arrow's shaft with wood-colored rods between calculated bottom and top points in the quiver, then adding a small glow tip and fletching cards near the top of each shaft.

Still writing feather SVG...

I'm deciding the fletching orientation near the nock end, adding a glow sphere at the arrow's tail, and sketching out the quiver's leather texture with gold tooled bands, skipping the strap rings for now. Moving to the bow, I'm placing small teal gem runes as octahedron geometry along the limb positions near the wrist area.

Now I'm positioning the bowstring as a rod running between the tip coordinates, matching the bow path's endpoints and giving it a thin cream-colored radius, while deciding to skip the nock cones and serving wrap details for simplicity.

I need a sweep helper for the bow curve using Catmull-Rom points, with band fills for the grip wrap and gold accents, plus point caps at both ends. Now I'm setting up the arm geometry, computing shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions symmetrically for each side.

Building arm chains with Catmull paths...

Mapping out the wrist region: skin shows below the cream sleeve, with leather bracer bands wrapping the forearm and a small gold ring loop near the elbow bend.

For the rings, I'm looping around the arm surface at each parametric point along its length, using the arm's tangent direction so the bands sit naturally against the bend. I'll place five leather rings plus two gold accent rings at the ends, each swept as a closed path with its own radius and color.

Now I'm moving on to the hand geometry, building a capsule shape between the wrist and hand endpoint tied to the wrist joint. I'm computing the hand's orientation using vectors derived from the elbow-to-wrist direction, projecting a side normal and crossing it to get a width vector, checking that the sign flips correctly for left versus right arms so the palm faces the right way.

Setting up finger segments...

Defining thumb geometry...

Now thinking about the pauldron lathe shape and how to properly type the outline points array for the builder API.

Defining dome and rim geometry...

Adding P3 with radius .105, checking plate coverage against the arm position. I'll keep pauldrons symmetrical left and right rather than making the elven rangers asymmetrical, and settle on a green leather plate color with a gold rim for the pauldron cap.

Now for hair: I'm defining a grained paint texture streaking vertically, then placing a hair cap sphere on the head bone scaled down to sit tightly over the skull.
